outages.place: Southern Odisha, including Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, Kandhamal, and Boudh
outages.affected: TPSODL, as reported by OdishaBytes and Odisha Ray on Nov 20, 2026, said it had restored electricity supply to 1,069,026 consumers (written as 10,69,026 in those reports) after Cyclone Akvan made landfall near Gopalpur on Friday morning, achieving 98.68 percent restoration — nearly 99 percent — across its eight-district operational area within seven hours. Those reports said all six affected 33 kV feeders, all 19 affected 33/11 kV power substations, and all 42 affected power transformers were restored, and that 364 of 365 affected 11 kV feeders and 35,749 affected distribution transformers had been restored. District-wise restoration was reported as 99.76 percent in Ganjam, 99.53 percent in Koraput, 98.90 percent in Gajapati, 98.06 percent in Rayagada, 98.01 percent in Nabarangpur, 97.55 percent in Boudh, 94.23 percent in Kandhamal, and 100 percent in Malkangiri. TPSODL CEO Amit Kumar Garg, quoted in those reports, said the company had achieved nearly 99 percent restoration. An earlier Nov 20 Odisha Stand report from Berhampur said TPSODL had reported that Cyclone Akvan affected 1,083,348 consumers across its operational area, including 534,361 in Ganjam district and 123,252 in Nabarangpur district. Later Nov 20 articles, including Odisha News Online from Berhampur, described Garg visiting cyclone-affected areas of Ganjam to review restoration and restated the same 1,083,348 affected-consumer total, including the Ganjam and Nabarangpur district figures, but did not give a later remaining-outage count or a later restoration percentage after the 98.68 percent figure. No official remaining-outage count, and no official estimated time for full restoration of remaining customers, was stated in the later OdishaBytes and Odisha Ray reports. A New Indian Express report updated at 3:39 a.m. IST Saturday, Nov 21 (4:09 p.m. CT Friday) said power supply was disrupted in parts of the state due to the storm, with restoration work underway on a war footing in several areas of northern Odisha, including Bhadrak, Balasore and Mayurbhanj. That report did not give an official remaining-outage count for those northern districts or a later TPSODL remaining-outage count. No later official remaining-outage count or official notice of full restoration from TPSODL, TPNODL, or the Odisha government was found as of 6:00 AM CT Saturday (5:30 p.m. IST Saturday, Nov 21).
outages.start: Morning of Nov 20, 2026 (IST), when Cyclone Akvan made landfall near Gopalpur
outages.updated: Nov 20–21, 2026, TPSODL figures via OdishaBytes and Odisha Ray (Nov 20); earlier TPSODL affected total via Odisha Stand (Nov 20); CEO restoration review via Odisha News Online (Nov 20), which restated the same affected total and did not give a later remaining-outage count; New Indian Express report updated 3:39 a.m. IST Saturday, Nov 21 (= 4:09 p.m. CT Friday), on restoration work in northern Odisha including Bhadrak, Balasore and Mayurbhanj, with no official customer count; rechecked 6:00 AM CT Saturday (5:30 p.m. IST Saturday), no later official remaining-outage count or official notice of full restoration from TPSODL, TPNODL, or the Odisha government found

outages.cause: Rolling and emergency blackouts after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure, including a large-scale overnight and morning attack on Nov 20 and further strikes reported on Nov 21
outages.affected: Ukrenergo, as reported by LB.ua at 6:43 p.m. EET Friday, Nov 20 (10:43 a.m. CT) and by UNIAN at 7:18 p.m. and 8:55 p.m. EET Friday (11:18 a.m. and 12:55 p.m. CT), said that on Saturday, Nov 21, planned electricity outages would be in effect around the clock in parts of the country because of the aftermath of attacks on the power system. Ukrenergo said all categories of consumers would face hourly outage schedules of 1.5 to 3 groups, and that industry would face capacity-restriction schedules. UNIAN, citing Ukrenergo, said those 1.5 to 3 queues for household consumers should correspond to outages of 6 to 12 hours, and that the hourly schedules for the public and the industrial restrictions would both run throughout Saturday. Those Saturday schedules remained the latest nationwide Ukrenergo schedule found at the time of this update (2:00 p.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21, which is 6:00 AM CT Saturday). KyivPost, in a report published at 11:45 a.m. EET Saturday (3:45 a.m. CT), citing DTEK, the Vinnytsia regional military administration, and the Rivne regional administration, said that after Russian attacks, part of Vinnytsia and 50 settlements in Rivne region remained without power, that emergency outages had been introduced on Saturday morning in Dnipropetrovsk region, and that emergency outages introduced on Saturday morning in Odesa and part of Odesa district had later been cancelled, with stabilization (scheduled) outage schedules restored there. No official nationwide customer count was given in those Saturday reports. Earlier Friday context remains as previously reported: Ukraine's Energy Ministry, in a statement reported by Ukrinform at 1:41 p.m. EET Friday, Nov 20 (5:41 a.m. CT), said that during the night and morning Russia had launched another large-scale attack on critical energy infrastructure — power plants and substations of electricity transmission and distribution systems — and that nuclear power plants were forced to reduce their generation capacity. As of Friday morning, the ministry said, some consumers remained without power in the city of Kyiv and in the Vinnytsia, Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, Kirovohrad, Odesa, Kharkiv, Kherson, Cherkasy, and Chernihiv regions. DTEK, as reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 9:38 p.m. EET Friday (1:38 p.m. CT), said that during the night and morning Russia had launched more than 400 strike drones and more than 110 missiles at Ukraine, and that targets included power plants and substations. No official nationwide customer count was given. A recheck at 6:00 AM CT Saturday (2:00 p.m. EET Saturday) found no official nationwide customer count and no later official change to the Saturday all-day Ukrenergo schedules.
outages.updated: Nov 20–21, 2026, KyivPost 11:45 a.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21 (= 3:45 a.m. CT) citing DTEK, Vinnytsia regional military administration, and Rivne regional administration on Saturday morning outages in Vinnytsia, Rivne region, Dnipropetrovsk region, and Odesa; Ukrenergo Saturday Nov 21 all-day schedules via LB.ua 6:43 p.m. EET Friday (= 10:43 a.m. CT) and UNIAN 7:18 p.m. and 8:55 p.m. EET Friday (= 11:18 a.m. and 12:55 p.m. CT), which remained the latest nationwide schedules found; DTEK via Interfax-Ukraine 9:38 p.m. EET Friday (= 1:38 p.m. CT); Energy Ministry via Ukrinform 1:41 p.m. EET Friday (= 5:41 a.m. CT); rechecked 6:00 AM CT Saturday (2:00 p.m. EET Saturday), no official nationwide customer count and no later official change to those Saturday schedules found

outages.cause: Russian attacks on energy infrastructure, including a large-scale overnight and morning attack on Nov 20. On Saturday, Nov 21, DTEK said emergency outages had again been introduced, on Ukrenergo's order, in Dnipro city and in the Dniprovskyi, Samarivskyi, Pavlohradskyi, and Kamianskyi districts, and that hourly schedules did not apply there
outages.affected: Ukrinform, in a report published at 10:36 a.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21 (2:36 a.m. CT), citing DTEK Group in Telegram, said emergency electricity outages had been introduced in Dnipropetrovsk region on Ukrenergo's order. It said the emergency outages were in effect in Dnipro and in the Dniprovskyi, Samarivskyi, Pavlohradskyi, and Kamianskyi districts, and that during emergency outages the hourly schedules did not apply. Censor.NET, in a 10:49 a.m. EET Saturday report (2:49 a.m. CT) also citing DTEK, gave the same list of places and likewise quoted DTEK as saying that during emergency outages the schedules do not apply, and that the company would report any changes in its Telegram channel. KyivPost, at 11:45 a.m. EET Saturday (3:45 a.m. CT), likewise said emergency outages had been introduced on Saturday morning in part of Dnipropetrovsk region and that the schedules did not apply in Dnipro and those four districts. Those Saturday emergency outages were the latest official status found at the time of this update (2:00 p.m. EET Saturday). No official customer count for Dnipro or Dnipropetrovsk region was given in those Saturday statements. Earlier Friday, DTEK, as reported by Ukrainska Pravda at 10:26 a.m. EET Friday, Nov 20 (2:26 a.m. CT), said at 8:47 a.m. EET Friday (12:47 a.m. CT) that emergency outages had been introduced in part of Dnipropetrovsk region, and that in Dnipro city and in the Dnipro, Samarivka, Pavlohrad, and Kamianske districts emergency outages were in effect and hourly schedules did not apply. Ukraine's Energy Ministry, as reported by Ukrinform at 1:41 p.m. EET Friday (5:41 a.m. CT), said that as of Friday morning some consumers in Dnipropetrovsk region remained without power. The latest official customer count found remains DTEK's Tuesday-morning figure. Suspilne, citing DTEK's Telegram page in an 11:18 a.m. EET Tuesday, Nov 17 report, said that after new large-scale Russian strikes on the region's energy infrastructure that morning, significant damage to energy facilities left 700,000 homes without power in Dnipro and the Dniprovskyi, Pavlohradskyi, Kamianskyi, and Samarivskyi districts. Censor.NET, also citing DTEK in an 11:22 a.m. Tuesday report, said 700,000 families were left without power in the region and likewise named those districts. No official restoration time was given. No later official customer count after the Tuesday-morning 700,000-household figure was found as of 6:00 AM CT Saturday (2:00 p.m. EET Saturday).
outages.start: Morning of Nov 17, 2026 (Kyiv time), after earlier attacks on the evening of Nov 16
outages.updated: Nov 21, 2026, DTEK via Ukrinform 10:36 a.m. EET Saturday (= 2:36 a.m. CT) and Censor.NET 10:49 a.m. EET Saturday (= 2:49 a.m. CT) on Saturday emergency outages in Dnipro and four districts, with hourly schedules not applying; KyivPost 11:45 a.m. EET Saturday (= 3:45 a.m. CT); earlier Friday DTEK via Ukrainska Pravda 10:26 a.m. EET Friday (= 2:26 a.m. CT), citing DTEK at 8:47 a.m. EET Friday (= 12:47 a.m. CT); Energy Ministry via Ukrinform 1:41 p.m. EET Friday (= 5:41 a.m. CT); Tuesday-morning 700,000-household figure, DTEK via Suspilne and Censor.NET; rechecked 6:00 AM CT Saturday (2:00 p.m. EET Saturday), no later official customer count after the Tuesday-morning 700,000-household figure found

outages.cause: Russian attack on a DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi energy facility on the morning of Nov 20. DTEK's official Friday evening statement also said weather-damage cleanup was continuing in the region. KyivPost, citing DTEK, said emergency outages were introduced in Odesa and part of Odesa district on Saturday morning, Nov 21, and were later cancelled, with stabilization schedules restored
outages.affected: DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi, in an official Nov 20 evening statement titled "Situation with electricity as of the evening of November 20," said that after the morning enemy attack the situation in Odesa and the region remained controlled, that all critical-infrastructure facilities had been energized, that stabilization (scheduled) outage schedules were in effect, and that electricity was gradually returning to homes. It said repair work on energy facilities was continuing, and that power had been restored in part of the Odesa and Rozdilna districts after the morning shelling of substations. It said 8,000 families in 21 settlements remained without power, that temporary voltage drops were possible during the work, and that restoration was being made extremely difficult by continuous air-raid alerts in the region. The same official statement said weather-damage cleanup was also continuing in the region: during the day specialists had restored power for 37,700 families, and DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi crews would work overnight to restore power to another 15,600 families in 55 villages and towns. The company did not add the 8,000 and 15,600 figures together and did not announce a firm time for full restoration. Earlier Friday, 41,000 households were without power in the Odesa and Rozdilna districts, according to DTEK's press service as reported by Ukrainska Pravda at 11:27 a.m. EET Friday, Nov 20 (3:27 a.m. CT), and by Ekonomichna Pravda at 10:55 a.m. EET Friday (2:55 a.m. CT). KyivPost, in a report published at 11:45 a.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21 (3:45 a.m. CT), citing DTEK, said emergency outages had also been introduced on Saturday morning in Odesa and part of Odesa district and that those emergency outages had later been cancelled, with a return to stabilization (scheduled) outage schedules. A recheck of DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi's public news list found no later official remaining-customer-count statement after the Friday evening statement. No later official remaining customer count after that official evening statement was found as of 6:00 AM CT Saturday (2:00 p.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21).
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given. The official Friday evening statement said repair work after the morning attack was continuing, and that crews would work overnight to restore power to another 15,600 families in 55 villages and towns (the weather-related figure in that statement). That is not an official firm time for full restoration. No later official firm restoration time was found.
outages.updated: Nov 20–21, 2026, DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi official Friday evening statement on remaining 8,000 families after the morning attack and on 15,600 families still to be restored overnight after weather damage; KyivPost 11:45 a.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21 (= 3:45 a.m. CT), citing DTEK, on Saturday morning emergency outages in Odesa and part of Odesa district later being cancelled and stabilization schedules restored; earlier Friday morning 41,000-household figure, DTEK press service via Ukrainska Pravda 11:27 a.m. EET Friday (= 3:27 a.m. CT) and Ekonomichna Pravda 10:55 a.m. EET Friday (= 2:55 a.m. CT); rechecked 6:00 AM CT Saturday (2:00 p.m. EET Saturday), no later official remaining count after the Friday evening statement found on the company's public news list

outages.cause: Russian attack that seriously damaged energy equipment in Sarny district. Rivneoblenergo said hourly outage schedules did not apply because this was an emergency outage from the damage
outages.affected: Oleksandr Koval, head of the Rivne regional military administration, as reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 1:04 a.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21 (5:04 p.m. CT Friday), said that as a result of a Russian attack on Sarny district in Rivne region, 50 settlements had been left without electricity, and that constant air-raid alerts were preventing energy workers from promptly repairing the damage. Interfax-Ukraine quoted Koval's Telegram post as saying, "Half a hundred settlements have been de-energized as a result of an enemy attack on Sarny district. Constant alerts do not allow energy workers to promptly eliminate the consequences of the strike." ITV Media Group, in a report published at 10:24 a.m. EET Saturday (2:24 a.m. CT), citing Rivneoblenergo, said that as a result of another enemy attack and serious damage to energy equipment, 46 settlements in Sarny district remained without electricity. Rivneoblenergo, as quoted in that report, said hourly outage schedules did not apply in this situation and that this was an emergency de-energization because of damaged energy equipment, and that its specialists had been working since the previous evening to eliminate the consequences of the attack. KyivPost, at 11:45 a.m. EET Saturday (3:45 a.m. CT), likewise said about 50 settlements in Sarny district remained without power after Russian strikes, and quoted Koval as saying constant alerts were not allowing energy workers to promptly eliminate the consequences of the strike. No official customer count was given. No official firm restoration time was given. No later official remaining-settlement or customer count after the Saturday morning Rivneoblenergo figure of 46 settlements was found as of 6:00 AM CT Saturday (2:00 p.m. EET Saturday).
outages.start: Evening of Nov 20, 2026 (Kyiv time), according to Rivneoblenergo as reported by ITV Media Group
outages.updated: Nov 21, 2026, Rivneoblenergo via ITV Media Group 10:24 a.m. EET Saturday (= 2:24 a.m. CT) on 46 settlements in Sarny district still without power and on emergency rather than scheduled outages; Oleksandr Koval, Rivne regional military administration, via Interfax-Ukraine 1:04 a.m. EET Saturday (= 5:04 p.m. CT Friday) on 50 settlements; KyivPost 11:45 a.m. EET Saturday (= 3:45 a.m. CT); rechecked 6:00 AM CT Saturday (2:00 p.m. EET Saturday), no later official remaining-settlement or customer count and no official firm restoration time found

outages.place: Kurdistan Region, including Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, Duhok, Bazian, and Chamchamal
outages.cause: Suspected drone attack on the Khor Mor gas field on the night of Nov 8, 2026, which halted gas production that supplies much of the region's electricity generation. Dana Gas, the field's operator, later said the facility had sustained significant damage and could produce no gas
outages.affected: Al Jazeera, on Nov 9, 2026, citing Iraqi and Kurdish officials, said a Sunday-night drone attack on the Khor Mor gas field caused a fire and left more than 70 percent of the Kurdish region without power. Omid Ahmed (also spelled Omed Ahmed), spokesperson for the Kurdistan Regional Government's Ministry of Electricity, said the attack suspended gas supply to power plants in Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, Bazian, Chamchamal, and Duhok, and knocked between 2,500 and 2,800 megawatts of generation off the grid, Al Jazeera reported, citing the official Iraqi News Agency (INA). Rudaw later quoted Ahmed as saying that authorities had increased generation from approximately 1,000 megawatts immediately after the attack to 1,550 megawatts, of which 50 megawatts were reserved for essential facilities and factories, leaving 1,500 megawatts for residents and raising daily public electricity supply to six to eight hours, reaching nine hours in some areas. Ahmed said the electricity then available covered only 40 percent of the region's demand, leaving a 60 percent shortfall, and that no date had been established for production to resume. Rudaw's article image assets for that report are dated Nov 13, 2026. Dana Gas, in a Saturday statement reported by Rudaw, said the facility had sustained significant damage and that currently no amount of gas could be produced. Later reports, including The Thursday Times on Nov 15, 2026, and QC Intel's account that the field was still offline one week after the attack, likewise said production remained shut. 964media, in a Nov 15 report, quoted Ahmed as saying that no timeframe had been set for electricity supplies to return to normal and that the ministry was waiting for gas from Khor Mor to flow again; in that interview he also said that within 48 hours of the attack the ministry had increased generation from 1,000 megawatts to nearly 1,650 megawatts, and that some areas were then getting more than eight hours of grid power a day, particularly on holidays. No official customer count was given. No later official generation figure, public-supply-hours update, or official confirmation that Khor Mor production had resumed was found as of 6:00 AM CT Saturday, Nov 21.
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given. As of the latest official statements found, no date had been established for Khor Mor production to resume.
outages.updated: Nov 8–16, 2026 attack and aftermath: Al Jazeera Nov 9 citing Iraqi and Kurdish officials and INA; KRG electricity ministry figures via Rudaw (article image assets dated Nov 13); Dana Gas still-shut statement via Rudaw, The Thursday Times Nov 15, and QC Intel one-week-after account; Omed Ahmed via 964media Nov 15 on no timeframe for a return to normal supply and on generation rising to nearly 1,650 megawatts within 48 hours of the attack; rechecked 6:00 AM CT Saturday, Nov 21, no later official generation figure or confirmation that Khor Mor production had resumed found

outages.place: Donetsk, Makiivka, Mariupol, Horlivka, Yenakiieve, Debaltseve, Snizhne, and nearby districts
outages.cause: Local accidents and a power deficit, according to the occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy. The ministry said a failure in electrical-network equipment in Donetsk around 7:00 p.m. Friday, Nov 20, left part of the city without power, and that repair work was interrupted overnight because of darkness and a continuing UAV-attack threat
outages.affected: The occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, in a Saturday morning statement reported by DNR News at 10:12 a.m. Saturday, Nov 21 (1:12 a.m. CT if the time is Moscow time), and citing Donetskenergo, a branch of JSC South-West Electric Grid Company, said that as of 7:00 a.m. Saturday, Nov 21 (10:00 p.m. CT Friday if that time is Moscow time), more than 107,000 subscribers in the occupied region remained without power. It said some consumers had already been reconnected after repair work. The same statement said that around 7:00 p.m. Friday, Nov 20 (10:00 a.m. CT Friday if Moscow time), a failure in electrical-network equipment had left part of Donetsk without electricity; that energy workers began restoration work that evening but could not continue overnight because of darkness and a continuing UAV-attack threat; and that work resumed at first light, with completion and a staged reconnection of consumers expected in the coming hours. It said partial outages also continued in other localities because of a shortage of available capacity and local emergency situations, affecting Makiivka, Mariupol, Yenakiieve, Horlivka, Debaltseve, and the Yasynuvata, Amvrosiivka, Volnovakha, Telmanove, and Volodarske municipal districts. It said the situation in Snizhne remained difficult because that city's supply also depends on power transfers from occupied Luhansk, and that after talks with occupation authorities there, some previously disconnected consumers had been reconnected on the evening of Nov 20. A later DNR News report at 11:39 a.m. Saturday (2:39 a.m. CT if Moscow time), also citing the occupation ministry, restated that more than 107,000 subscribers remained without power and that the cause was local accidents and a power deficit. Occupation city head Aleksey Kulemzin, as reported by News.ru at 11:42 a.m. Saturday (2:42 a.m. CT if Moscow time), said more than 67,000 subscribers in Donetsk remained without power because of network overloads and emergency outages. News.ru quoted Kulemzin as saying that, according to Donetskenergo, 392 transformer substations had automatically disconnected in parts of the Kyivskyi, Voroshylovskyi, Kirovskyi, Kuibyshevskyi, Proletarskyi, and Kalininskyi districts. No later official region-wide remaining total after the 7:00 a.m. Saturday figure of more than 107,000 subscribers, and no later official city total after Kulemzin's more-than-67,000 figure, was found as of 6:00 AM CT Saturday (3:00 p.m. Moscow time Saturday).
outages.start: Around 7:00 p.m. Friday, Nov 20, 2026 (10:00 a.m. CT Friday if Moscow time), for the Donetsk city equipment failure described by the occupation ministry; other partial outages in the region were already being reported
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given. The occupation ministry said Saturday morning that completion of the Donetsk city repairs and a staged reconnection of consumers were expected in the coming hours. That is not an official firm time for full restoration of the more than 107,000 subscribers reported region-wide.
outages.updated: Nov 21, 2026, occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy via DNR News 10:12 a.m. Saturday (= 1:12 a.m. CT if Moscow time), citing Donetskenergo, on more than 107,000 subscribers remaining without power as of 7:00 a.m. Saturday (= 10:00 p.m. CT Friday if Moscow time), and on the Friday 7:00 p.m. Donetsk city equipment failure; DNR News 11:39 a.m. Saturday (= 2:39 a.m. CT if Moscow time) restating the more-than-107,000 figure and attributing outages to local accidents and a power deficit; occupation city head Aleksey Kulemzin via News.ru 11:42 a.m. Saturday (= 2:42 a.m. CT if Moscow time) on more than 67,000 subscribers remaining without power in Donetsk and on 392 substations automatically disconnecting; rechecked 6:00 AM CT Saturday (3:00 p.m. Moscow time Saturday), no later official region-wide remaining total found

outages.place: Crimea, including Dzhankoy, Yevpatoria, and Bilohirsk
outages.cause: Occupation utility Krymenergo said Saturday, Nov 21, that restrictions on electricity-consumption regimes had been introduced and that localities would be left without power for three to six hours. Occupation authorities, as reported by RIA Novosti Crimea, have said a power deficit on the peninsula began after Oct 24 attacks on transmission networks outside the peninsula, which those sources attributed to Ukrainian drones; that attribution was not independently confirmed
outages.affected: No official customer count was given. RIA Novosti Crimea, in a report published at 9:06 a.m. Saturday, Nov 21 (12:06 a.m. CT if the time is Moscow time), citing Krymenergo, said that on Saturday restrictions on electricity-consumption regimes had been introduced in Crimea and that electricity supply in localities on the peninsula would be temporarily stopped, with an approximate duration of 3 to 6 hours. It quoted Krymenergo as saying that if the outage periods were extended or additional restrictions were introduced, further information would be published. The same report said that as of Saturday morning there was no electricity in Bilohirsk and in Rozdolne and Sovietskyi districts, and that supply to those subscribers was planned to be restored in three hours. RIA Novosti Crimea, in a later report published at 11:40 a.m. Saturday (2:40 a.m. CT if Moscow time), also citing Krymenergo, said that on Saturday six districts and three cities had been left without power for approximately three hours because of the introduced restrictions. It said there was no power in the villages of Berezovka, Ulyanovka, Orlovka, Kashtanovka, and Bakhchevka in Rozdolne district; in Sovietskyi district, including the urban-type settlement of Sovietskyi and Krasnoflotskoye, Shakhtino, Markovo, Urozhainoye, Prisivashnoye, Chapayevka, Novy Mir, Nikolayevka, Nekrasovka, Rovenky, Dmitrovka, Chernozyomnoye, Demyanovka, Almaznoye, Razdolnoye, Korneevka, and Oktyabrskoye; in Saky district, including Mikhailovka, Orekhovo, Shtormovoye, Khutorok, Vitino, Romashkino, Abrikosovka, Shishkino, Furmanovo, and Vorobyovo; in Pervomaiske district, including Levitanovka, Kalinino, Grishino, and Frunze; in Kirovske district, including Kirovske, Yarkoye Pole, Shubino, and Tokarevo; and in Dzhankoy district, including Izumrudnoye and Luganskoye. It said there was no power on 75 streets and lanes in Dzhankoy, on 36 streets in Yevpatoria, and on 44 streets and in three garden associations in Bilohirsk. The same report restated that Saturday restrictions would leave localities without power for three to six hours. Occupation sources, as summarized in the earlier RIA Novosti Crimea reports, have said interruptions in Crimea and Sevastopol began on Oct 24, when they said drones attacked transmission networks outside the peninsula, and that a further attack on energy facilities affecting the peninsula was made on the night of Nov 4; those accounts and attributions come from occupation sources and were not independently confirmed. No official customer count or firm restoration time for the Saturday restrictions as a whole was given. A later recheck at 6:00 AM CT Saturday (3:00 p.m. Moscow time Saturday, Nov 21) found no later official customer count and no later official list of de-energized localities after the 11:40 a.m. Saturday RIA Novosti Crimea report.
outages.start: Occupation sources said peninsula-wide interruptions began Oct 24, 2026; Saturday's additional 3-to-6-hour restrictions were reported Nov 21, 2026
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given for the Saturday restrictions as a whole. Krymenergo, as reported by RIA Novosti Crimea, said Saturday's restrictions would leave localities without power for three to six hours, and that the Saturday-morning outages in Bilohirsk and in Rozdolne and Sovietskyi districts were planned to be restored in three hours.
outages.updated: Nov 21, 2026, Krymenergo via RIA Novosti Crimea 11:40 a.m. Saturday (= 2:40 a.m. CT if Moscow time) on six districts and three cities, including 75 streets and lanes in Dzhankoy, 36 streets in Yevpatoria, and 44 streets and three garden associations in Bilohirsk, left without power for approximately three hours; Krymenergo via RIA Novosti Crimea 9:06 a.m. Saturday (= 12:06 a.m. CT if Moscow time) on Saturday 3-to-6-hour restrictions and on Saturday-morning outages in Bilohirsk and Rozdolne and Sovietskyi districts, planned for three hours; rechecked 6:00 AM CT Saturday (3:00 p.m. Moscow time Saturday), no later official customer count and no later official list of de-energized localities found

outages.cause: Generation capacity deficit, with several thermoelectric units offline due to breakdowns and maintenance. UNE's Friday bulletin said that unit 8 of CTE Mariel, unit 1 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 2 of CTE Felton, and unit 6 of CTE Renté were in breakdown, and that unit 3 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 5 of CTE Nuevitas, unit 1 of CTE Felton, and unit 5 of CTE Renté were in maintenance
outages.affected: UNE's Friday bulletin, published by Cubadebate on Friday, Nov 20, and also reported by Granma, Directorio Cubano, and Limonada 24/7 citing Cubadebate, remains the latest official national forecast found: if forecast conditions hold, 1,835 MW affected at the evening peak, with 1,045 MW available versus 2,850 MW of demand (a 1,805 MW deficit). At 6:00 a.m. Cuba time Friday (5:00 a.m. CT), the grid had 1,000 MW available versus 2,250 MW of demand, leaving 1,242 MW unserved, and UNE estimated 1,350 MW affected at midday. On Thursday, service was affected by a generation-capacity deficit for all 24 hours and remained affected through the early morning Friday; the maximum Thursday affectation was 1,789 MW at 6:50 p.m. Cuba time Thursday (5:50 p.m. CT Thursday). Thursday solar photovoltaic output was 4,320 MWh, with a maximum of 672 MW. The Friday bulletin said unit 8 of CTE Mariel, unit 1 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 2 of CTE Felton, and unit 6 of CTE Renté were in breakdown, and that unit 3 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 5 of CTE Nuevitas, unit 1 of CTE Felton, and unit 5 of CTE Renté were in maintenance. It said thermal generation limitations were 368 MW, and that unit 8 of Mariel was expected to enter at the evening peak with 45 MW. Official UNE sources did not report a total collapse of the national grid. No official Friday evening-peak actual from UNE, and no official Saturday national UNE bulletin, was found as of 6:00 AM CT Saturday (7:00 a.m. Cuba time Saturday, Nov 21). The Empresa Eléctrica de La Habana, as compiled by CiberCuba on its Saturday, Nov 21 outage page, updated at 6:15 a.m. Cuba time Saturday (5:15 a.m. CT), said that at 6:01 a.m. Cuba time Saturday (5:01 a.m. CT) 108 distribution circuits were affected and the affectation was 221 MW, due to a generation deficit. That page also cited Saturday-morning circuit interruptions beginning at 6:05 a.m. Cuba time Saturday (5:05 a.m. CT), including circuits R453, R466, R461, and S516, and said the provincial company had also reported some restorations during the early morning. Those Havana circuit and megawatt figures are not an official nationwide evening-peak actual. Earlier Friday Havana figures, as compiled by CiberCuba, included 133 circuits and 327 MW affected at 12:04 a.m. Cuba time Saturday, Nov 21 (11:04 p.m. CT Friday), 133 circuits and 315 MW at 9:00 p.m. Cuba time Friday (8:00 p.m. CT), and 147 circuits and 330 MW at 6:00 p.m. Cuba time Friday (5:00 p.m. CT).

outages.cause: Drone attacks on power stations and other electricity infrastructure during the war between the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces
outages.affected: No official customer count. A United Nations report published Nov 17, issued in Geneva and posted on the UN in Sudan website, said that in just over two weeks between Oct 20 and Nov 4, 29 drone strikes, attributed to the Rapid Support Forces, hit electricity facilities and fuel stations across 11 states, triggering widespread power blackouts and further fuel shortages affecting millions far from the conflict frontlines. It said the strikes had a devastating impact on civilians and essential services, causing power outages that disrupted health services including dialysis and surgical procedures, access to clean water, and food production. AFP, in a Nov 17 report on the same OHCHR findings, likewise said the intensification of drone strikes targeting power stations and fuel supplies had become a worrying trend, and quoted the report as saying that between Oct 20 and Nov 4 some 29 drone strikes attributed to the RSF hit electricity facilities and fuel stations, triggering widespread power blackouts and further fuel shortages affecting millions far from the conflict frontlines. That official humanitarian account is later than an Al Jazeera Nov 15 feature, which said the RSF has intensified attacks on power stations around Khartoum state over the past month, creating an energy crisis in the capital, and that there is no clear schedule for the resulting power cuts, which can last anywhere between six hours and a day. Al Jazeera said that between Oct 20 and Nov 2, 2026, there were at least 18 attacks on electricity infrastructure across at least nine states, leading to declining power generation capacity and fuel shortages. Citing The Associated Press, it said repeated drone attacks on power stations have seen electricity generation fall from about 4,400 megawatts before the war to about 1,100 MW today. Residents and a small-business owner in Port Sudan described prolonged, unreliable cuts, including outages lasting more than 24 hours. The UN resident and humanitarian coordinator, Denise Brown, was quoted warning that repeated strikes on power and fuel stations were disrupting dialysis, hospital births, and operations. No later official national customer count or restoration timetable was found as of 6:00 AM CT Saturday.
